shots.phrase: Begin by framing Lesson Title: CSCI-620: Introduction to Big Data as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Consider this worked case: Case studies examine urban crime, drug research, census data, social networking, and space exploration.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Lesson Title: Lesson 1: Foundations of Big Data precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: Students must verify their prerequisite status before enrolling in the course.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how Lesson Title: Lesson 2: Internet Protocol Suite Overview operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: The link layer moves frames across a directly connected network, while IP provides best-effort datagram delivery across interconnected networks.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in Lesson Title: Lesson 3: IP Addressing and Routing and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: When a packet is sent, the router examines the IP address to determine the optimal path to the destination interface.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Lesson Title: Lesson 4: Transport Protocol Functions to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: Application protocols define the meaning of exchanged data, while transport protocols handle the reliable delivery mechanism.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Lesson Title: Lesson 5: TCP Reliability and Byte Streams, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: Sequence numbers identify positions in that byte stream, allowing the receiver to reconstruct the original data order.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Lesson Title: Lesson 6: TCP Acknowledgments and Retransmission with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Consider this worked case: If a packet is lost, the receiver sends an acknowledgment indicating the gap, prompting the sender to retransmit the missing data.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Lesson Title: Lesson 7: TCP Flow Control and State Management to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Consider this worked case: Before application data transfer, connection establishment synchronizes endpoint state to ensure both sides are ready.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Lesson Title: Lesson 8: Data Preparation and Visualization to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: Cleaning and organizing raw datasets allows analysts to identify patterns and trends through visual representations.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Lesson Title: Lesson 9: Statistics and Grouping/Prediction Techniques as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Consider this worked case: Statistical methods help quantify uncertainty, while grouping and prediction techniques identify clusters and forecast future values.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
